episodes.187754: A frontal boundary associated with an upper trough pushed through central California between the afternoon of February 20 and the morning of February 21. Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along the boundary and many locations in the San Joaquin Valley picked up an additional quarter to half inch of rainfall as a result. Several stations in the Sierra Nevada and adjacent foothills picked up an additional half inch to an inch of additional liquid precipitation with several SNOTEL stations north of Kings Canyon picking up an estimated 5 to 10 inches of new snowfall. The frontal boundary stalled over Kern County during the early morning of February 21 resulting in nuisance flooding along several highways. The showers ended by late morning.
episodes.188030: Two storm systems impacted central California From February 17 to 20. A quickly-moving cold front came through the region on the 17th, causing minor nuisance flooding and gusty winds. A second, deeper but slower moving, system followed the next day with widespread rain and gusty winds. A warm front associated with this low came through the region late on Sunday the 18th, followed by the associated cold front and associated thunderstorms on Monday the 19th. With the longer period of rainfall and soils being saturated, shallow landslides were reported across the region.
episodes.188074: Strong rainfall from the South Pacific Convergence occurred from February 10th through the 20th. WSO Pago Pago received 15.11 inches of rain, while the US Park Service Weather Station at Mount Tumu in Ofu recorded 13.28 inches during that time. This rainfall, combined with previous rain events, caused landslides throughout the territory. Bands of rain from Tropical Depression 10F, centered just to the southeast of American Samoa on the 13th and 14th, contributed to 6.82 inches of rainfall recorded at WSO Pago Pago for those two days.
episodes.189138: A storm system produced moderate to locally heavy rainfall across Orange and San Bernardino Counties, with lesser amounts farther south and east. Over an inch of rain fell across the aforementioned areas, with some locations seeing up to 3 inches of rain. One to two feet of snow fell across the San Bernardino County Mountains. While lesser rain fell across San Diego County, locally heavy rain rates lead to several traffic incidents.
episodes.189331: A winter storm mid-February brought several days of continued heavy snow, rain, and gusty winds. Periods of chain controls were observed in the mountains with local reports of flooding and minor wind damage.
episodes.192501: A third, powerful, winter storm brought significant impacts to Southwestern California. Rainfall totals ranged between 2 and 12 inches with the highest totals across southern Santa Barbara county and western Ventura county. With the heavy rainfall, numerous reports of flooding and mud/debris flows were reported. Also, some gusty winds were reported.

events.narrative: California Highway Patrol reports that Lane 5 on the US50 E and 15 Street offramp was flooded.
A mudslide was reported along Highway 1 at the intersection with Porto Marina.
Several inches of water were flowing over streets and spraying out of manhole covers near San Francisco City Hall.
Heavy rainfall generated a mudslide across Rotunda Mesa Road.
California Highway Patrol reports roadway flooding at 413 Southgate Drive.
Flash flooding was reported on Interstate 405 near Sepulveda Boulevard. One vehicles was disabled due to the flooding.
A large rock slide was reported across Malibu Canyon Road. Several vehicles experienced blown tires from the rocks on the roadway.
Two lanes on SR94 were flooded creating a major traffic jam. Multiple observation sites recorded rainfall rates of 0.30 to 0.50 inch per hour.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding on both lanes of Copus Rd. near Interstate 5.
California Highway Patrol reported mud from a mud slide covering two westbound lanes of SR 58 at Comanche Dr.
California Highway Patrol reported the offramp flooded on SR 99 at the Copus Rd. exchange.
California Highway Patrol reported the offramp flooded on SR 99 at the SR 166 exchange.
California Highway Patrol reported SR 166 was closed at the intersection of Old River Rd. due to flooding.
Flash flooding resulted in the closure of Palmdale Boulevard between 70th street and 87th street.

A landslide occurred in the morning hours of February 21st along the main road in the village of Auto. Rocks and dirt covered both sides of the road, but the public reported that medium sized cars could pass through. The debris was cleared later in the morning.

A landslide occurred in the village of Amouli during the morning hours on February 21st. Rocks and dirt covered both westbound and eastbound lanes of the main road, which made it impassible. This is the only roadway to access Amouli and villages to the east of Amouli from the west side of the island. The debris was fully removed by the evening hours.
